clue.text: Old radio's last cry?

parts.note: the answer read as wordplay is a weeping sound followed by a jumbled version of a word for final, with the setting signalling the jumble, which gives the clue's two words

explanation.surface: A wistful question about the final sob of a vintage wireless.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: split the answer into CRY, STAL and SET, and SET is an anagram signal applied to STAL, giving LAST; so the answer encodes 'last cry'.
explanation.definitionFit: A crystal set is the simple early wireless receiver built around a crystal detector, so it is an old radio.

clue.text: Philistine's job, on the other hand, is a fake

parts.note: Philistine is the setter, so 'Philistine's' stands for 'the setter is', I'M
a post is a job or position
or introduces an alternative, as 'on the other hand' does

explanation.surface: The setter's work is condemned as counterfeit.
explanation.walkthrough: Philistine is the name of this puzzle's setter, so 'Philistine's' is I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: An impostor pretends to be someone else, so such a person is a fake or sham.

clue.text: Against Lewis larking about

parts.note: anti means opposed to, against
C. S. Lewis, author of the Narnia books, gives his initials CS

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a man called Lewis fooling around.
explanation.definitionFit: Antics are playful or silly capers, which is what larking about involves.

clue.text: Jacques Derrida served up wines for communists

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the selected letters read from bottom to top
served says the philosopher's name serves out a run of its letters as the answer

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The French philosopher pours drinks for his left-wing comrades.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave the hidden word no indicator; 'served' signals it and 'up' the reversal. Two definitions share one wordplay: wines, and communists.
explanation.definitionFit: Red wines are commonly called reds, and communists are called Reds after the colour of their flag.

clue.text: Whereby patient session starts with therapist's bottom in designer chair amid wise pronouncement

definitions.text: Whereby patient session starts with therapist's bottom in designer chair amid wise pronouncement

indicators.note: starts asks for the opening letters of the words patient and session
amid says the following pieces sit between the two letters of the sounded word
pronouncement says the word wise is to be taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: wise spoken sounds like two letter Ys, 'Y's'

indicators.note: in says the last letter of the next word goes inside the rearranged chair
designer suggests something deliberately rearranged, so the letters of chair are reworked
bottom in a down clue points to the last letter of therapist's

explanation.surface: A description of a therapy session: the patient on a designer couch while the therapist utters wise words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designer' rearranges CHAIR into CHIAR; 'in' puts T, the bottom of therapist's, inside to give CHIATR; 'amid' places that between the two Ys sounded by 'wise'; 'starts' gives P and S at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychiatry is the medical practice through which a patient, in session with a doctor, is treated for mental disorder.

clue.text: Soldier is one of four captured by other side

indicators.note: captured by says the piece is held inside the rearranged side
other says the word side is to be made into a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a quad is one of quadruplets, one of four born together

explanation.surface: A soldier is one of four taken prisoner by the enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other' looks like it qualifies side, but it is the anagram signal, and 'captured by' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Squaddie is British slang for a private soldier in the army.

clue.text: Friend we would back may, at a stretch, be 16 at the front?

definitions.note: 16-across is the scruff of the neck; the front of the neck is where this flap hangs

indicators.note: back says the combined pieces are read in reverse, upwards in this down clue

parts.note: a pal is a friend
we would contracts to we'd, the letters WED

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about a friend who might be persuaded to stand at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may, at a stretch, be' is the link: the fold of skin is on the neck's front, while 16, the scruff, is at its back, so the definition is loose and the question mark admits it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dewlap is the loose fold of skin hanging under the throat, the front of the neck.

clue.text: In obstetrics, is it best to ignore the odds and take no action?

indicators.note: In says the answer sits as a run of letters inside the word obstetrics

explanation.surface: A medical worry: in childbirth, is the best course to wait and do nothing?
explanation.walkthrough: A second wordplay also gives the answer: 'is it best' with its odd letters ignored leaves S, T, E, T.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet is the proofreader's instruction meaning 'let it stand', telling the editor to make no change.

clue.text: They are not being true lovers

definitions.meaning: people who romance in the sense of telling fanciful tales are not being truthful
those who romance someone are wooers or lovers

explanation.definitionFit: To romance is both to woo and to embellish or invent stories, so the noun covers fantasists and wooers.

clue.text: Search for something in the baroque style

indicators.note: something in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is hunting for an object decorated in the ornate baroque manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A quest is a long search for something, often in legend.

clue.text: Gold pens hide fiction

indicators.note: hide says one piece is kept concealed inside the other

parts.note: sties are pens for pigs
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Golden fountain pens are used to conceal made-up tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Stories are tales, which as invented narratives are fiction.

clue.text: In-house pansies, primarily as flower arrangement

indicators.note: In says the next piece goes inside the word for a house

parts.note: a chalet is a type of house, Swiss in style

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letter of pansies

explanation.surface: An instruction for an indoor floral display made mostly of pansies.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplet is a wreath or garland of flowers worn on the head.

clue.text: They appear in recital to sing

definitions.text: They appear in recital to sing

indicators.note: appear in says the answer shows up as a run of letters within the clue's following words

explanation.surface: Low female voices perform in a recital.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'recitAL TO Sing', and the whole clue describes singers who take part in such recitals.
explanation.definitionFit: Altos are singers with the lower female or high male voice range who perform in concerts.

clue.text: Conveniently ignored area of revolting snot build-up? Not us!

indicators.note: revolting describes the letters overturned, rearranged into a new order
Not says letters must be taken away from the jumbled pool

parts.note: taken as written as anagram material
us read as U's, the plural of the letter U, gives two Us

explanation.surface: A disgusting mucus accumulation that we would rather not admit is ours.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: 'revolting' shuffles SNOT BUILD-UP, and 'Not us', read as 'not U's', takes out its two Us, leaving the nine letters to arrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A blind spot is a subject or area a person fails to see or chooses to overlook.

clue.text: Mostly, you and I grappled with problem protein, for one

indicators.note: grappled with suggests the letters wrestle into a new order
Mostly says the word you loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Two people wrestle with a tricky protein question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims YOU to YO; 'grappled with' then rearranges YO, I and PROBLEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Proteins are large molecules built from chains of amino acids, an example of a natural polymer.

clue.text: Seek asylum in UK, get a free settlement

indicators.note: settlement suggests the letters settling into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An asylum seeker in Britain hoping to be granted housing for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settlement' rearranges the letters of UK GET A FREE.
explanation.definitionFit: To take refuge is to find shelter or protection from danger, as a person seeking asylum does.

clue.text: By which to take control, organising checks often to incarcerate 50% of ruffians

indicators.note: to incarcerate says the rearranged letters hold the next piece inside them
organising says the letters of checks often are put into a new order
50% of asks for the first half of the word ruffians

explanation.surface: Advice to a police officer on how to round up and lock away troublemakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organising' rearranges CHECKS OFTEN, and 'to incarcerate' puts RUFF, half of ruffians, inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Grabbing someone by the back of the neck is the idiomatic way to seize and control them.

clue.text: Rummaged for a slice of pomme de terre frite from the east

indicators.note: from the east says the hidden letters are read backwards
a slice of says only a run of letters is cut from within the French words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone searched for a piece of French fried potato.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Rummaged for a slice of pomme' as the definition; only 'Rummaged' defines, 'for' links and 'a slice of' signals the hidden letters. 'from the east' reads 'de TERRE Frite' backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To ferret about is to search busily, as a ferret hunts in burrows, so it means rummaged.

clue.text: At the centre of next spy plot, free warrior and adventurer

indicators.note: At the centre of asks for the middle letter or letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A thriller set-up: a spy plot, a warrior and a daring traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: The middles are EX, P, LO, RE and R.
explanation.definitionFit: An explorer travels into unknown places, a classic adventurer.

clue.text: One possible choice for Hamlet appearing before jolly or unknown island town

parts.note: Hamlet's soliloquy weighs 'to be, or not to be', so to be is one choice
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
Y is one of the algebraic unknowns

explanation.surface: A tour of options for staging Hamlet before a cheerful or obscure island audience.
explanation.walkthrough: TOBERMORY is the main town on the Scottish island of Mull.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobermory is the colourful harbour town on the Isle of Mull in the Hebrides.

clue.text: Second-rate heel for shoe

parts.note: B is the grade below A, so second-rate
a heel is a rotter, a rogue

explanation.surface: A poor-quality heel for a shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heel' looks like part of the shoe but means a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is a sturdy leather shoe with decorative perforations.

clue.text: Reject one way or the other

indicators.note: one way or the other says the clue word, as a verb, is also read in the opposite direction

parts.note: as a verb, to reject is to repel, push away

explanation.surface: Turn something down, whichever way you look at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reject' does double duty: as a noun it defines the answer, an outcast; as a verb it means REPEL, which read 'the other way' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A leper, figuratively, is an outcast shunned by society, a social reject.

clue.text: Dropping preliminaries, sleep with newly-wed in storage space

indicators.note: Dropping preliminaries says each of the two words loses its opening letter

parts.note: slumber is sleep
a groom is a newly-wed man

explanation.surface: Skipping foreplay, a honeymooner sleeps in the box room.
explanation.walkthrough: Both SLUMBER and GROOM lose their first letters. A lumber room is a British name for a room used to store junk.
explanation.definitionFit: A lumber room is a room where unused furniture and odds and ends are kept, a storage space.

clue.text: Where birds breed round New Yorker circles

indicators.note: circles says the rearranged letters surround the next piece
New says the letters of Yorker are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: a round shape is like the letter O

explanation.surface: A description of a nesting site, with a New York local wandering round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Yorker' looks like a resident of New York; here 'New' rearranges YORKER, which 'circles' O.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookery is a colony of rooks, or other birds, where they nest and breed.

clue.text: See 21
Holiday item?

parts.note: the answer read as wordplay is a word for duration followed by an anagram signal, and rearranging that word gives the clue word item

explanation.surface: A question about something packed for a vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer split as TIME OFF tells you to rearrange TIME, which gives ITEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Time off is a break from work, such as a holiday or vacation.

clue.text: Donald Trump, the first American king

indicators.note: the first asks for the opening letter of Trump

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A claim that Donald Trump was the first American king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Donald Trump' looks like one name, but 'Donald' is the definition: Donald Tusk, former President of the European Council.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Tusk is the Polish politician who was Prime Minister of Poland and President of the European Council.

clue.text: Small part of what comes next said you fell in love head over heels

definitions.text: Small part of what comes next

indicators.note: fell in says the sounded letter drops inside the reworked word
head over heels says the leading letter of love tumbles back toward the end of the word

parts.note: taken as written before its first letter moves

indicators.note: said says the word you is taken as it sounds, the letter U

parts.note: you spoken sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: Someone, reading what comes next, says you fell deeply in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head over heels' moves the L of LOVE back to give OVLE; 'fell in' drops U, said as 'you', inside to give OVULE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovule is the small structure in a plant that becomes a seed after fertilisation, the next generation.

clue.text: Candy gadgeteers nod off

indicators.note: off says the remaining letters are thrown out of order
nod read as 'no D' says the letter D is removed

explanation.surface: Inventors drop off to sleep, sugar-rushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nod off' looks like falling asleep; read 'no D', it removes D from GADGETEERS, and 'off' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An Easter egg is a chocolate egg given at Easter, a piece of confectionery.
